title: Likes and praise are not demand

sections.skill: Explain why likes and praise are weak demand signals

questions.prompt: A post about a new candle got 3,000 likes and 2 sales. What does this most likely show?

choices.text: Many people noticed it, but few wanted to buy.
The likes prove sales will rise soon.
Demand is very strong because of the likes.
Likes and sales always move together.

questions.correct_answer: Many people noticed it, but few wanted to buy.
questions.intro: Likes, follows, views and compliments feel good, but they are weak signs of demand. They cost people nothing, so many people give them freely. A post with 2,000 likes may lead to zero sales. Followers can also be people who enjoy your content but will never buy, or accounts that are not real people. To judge demand, look for actions that cost the person something: purchases, deposits, bookings, or replies asking how to buy. Treat likes as a sign of attention, not of buying.
questions.feedback: Attention is not the same as buying.

questions.prompt: People stopping to look at a store window show what?
questions.correct_answer: Attention
questions.intro: Think of a store window. Many people stop to look at a pretty display; that is attention. Far fewer walk in, and fewer still buy. Online, a like is the same as glancing at the window. A business needs the people who walk in and pay. When you measure an idea, count the people who acted with money or real effort, not the people who glanced.
questions.feedback: Looking is attention.
